statement: You are given an array nums of non-negative integers and an integer d.

Split nums into two groups S1 and S2 so that every element goes into exactly one group. Count the splits where sum(S1) ≥ sum(S2) and sum(S1) − sum(S2) = d. Splits are told apart by which positions go into S1.
Return that count. The original problem asks for it modulo 10⁹ + 7; the inputs here are small enough that this never matters.

examples.explanation: The total is 7, so S1 must sum to 4 and S2 to 3. S1 can be {first 1, 3}, {second 1, 3} or {1, 1, 2}.
The total is 6, so S1 would have to sum to (6 + 1) / 2 = 3.5. No group of integers can, so there is no valid split.
